analysis.title: DB CoTD: A normal election
key_insights: Seats lost by the incumbent party in midterms have historically tracked the president's approval rating going into the vote, which in turn tends to track consumer confidence.

Trump's summer approval rating pointed to a roughly 40-seat Republican loss in the House versus other parties at the same point before previous midterms. Live trackers (NBC, CBS, The Economist and others) now suggest a loss of around 43 seats.
The report concludes this looks like a normal election by historical standards, and markets appear to have welcomed that normality with an emerging relief rally.
Worries ahead of US elections tend to look more concerning than they do immediately afterwards, and this election is following that pattern.
The S&P 500 has been higher one year after each of the last 22 midterms. 1938 and 1930 were the last exceptions.
The report says AI and Iran may still test the calm in the coming weeks and months, and that AI will determine whether the streak extends to 23.
Political uncertainty usually peaks before the vote, not after it.
risk_factors: AI developments could test the post-election calm and determine whether the S&P 500 streak of higher levels one year after midterms extends.
Iran-related developments could test the post-election calm.
geopolitical: Iran is named as a possible source of risk that could test the post-election calm.
